problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a supply chain inspection across seven regional warehouses:
Warehouse Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (143,154)
Warehouse Beta: Positioned at grid reference (193,0)
Warehouse Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (9,126)
Warehouse Delta: Positioned at grid reference (83,79)
Warehouse Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (119,12)
Warehouse Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (106,48)
Warehouse Eta: Positioned at grid reference (140,162)

The travel times between warehouses, measured in minutes, are as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 136.9 min
Alpha to Delta: 96.0 min
Alpha to Epsilon: 144.0 min
Alpha to Zeta: 112.3 min
Alpha to Eta: 8.5 min
Beta to Gamma: 223.0 min
Beta to Delta: 135.4 min
Beta to Epsilon: 75.0 min
Beta to Zeta: 99.4 min
Beta to Eta: 170.4 min
Gamma to Delta: 87.7 min
Gamma to Epsilon: 158.4 min
Gamma to Zeta: 124.5 min
Gamma to Eta: 135.9 min
Delta to Epsilon: 76.1 min
Delta to Zeta: 38.6 min
Delta to Eta: 100.7 min
Epsilon to Zeta: 38.3 min
Epsilon to Eta: 151.5 min
Zeta to Eta: 119.0 min

No direct transport link exists between Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta.
Furthermore, the inspection route must incorporate exactly one of two critical corridors: either the link between Warehouse Beta and Gamma, or the link between Warehouse Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel time for a circuit that visits each warehouse precisely once before returning to the point of origin.
